displayPattern: 7-segment display on a *CVC96 or *MVC96 two-stage furnace covered by IOG-2015L, including Amana AMVC96 and ACVC96: EE0
meaning: Furnace lockout after an excessive number of ignition retries (3 total): flame was not established, or flame was lost after it was established.
causes: Front cover pressure switch or condensate drainage problem
Igniter that needs replacement or realignment
Blocked flue piping, or piping with the wrong length, elbows or termination
Induced draft blower not performing properly
diySteps: Confirm the gas supply to the furnace is on

The manual says an EE0 lockout can reset after one hour, after a power interruption, or after the thermostat is lowered for 1 to 20 seconds. If the original problem is still there, the control returns to lockout
Technician: check the front cover pressure switch and drainage, realign or replace the igniter, clean the flame sensor if it is coated or oxidized, check the flue, and check the induced draft blower
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician if EE0 returns after the gas supply is confirmed. This chart is the two-stage *CVC96 / *MVC96 guide, not the single-stage GR9S96 list.
sourceTitle: Amana and Goodman *CVC96 / *MVC96 two-stage furnace installation instructions (IOG-2015L)
